name: Binaural Classical
description: Concert music for headphones: original pieces in classical styles that use the two ears as part of the score. Brass choirs answering from opposite galleries, a canon whose voices enter from around your head, a nocturne over a pad that spreads from the centre to all around you, divided violins after Tchaikovsky, a chorale placed by tiny delays, an adagio whose strings drift apart in cents, an organ split by partials, a rotating chorale and a delta-wave lullaby. Each sketch explains its trick in the comments. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Antiphonal Canzona
sketches.description: Venetian polychoral music: two brass choirs, one at each ear, answer each other bar by bar across a church, then join for the last four bars over a centred organ pedal and timpani.

sketches.name: Canon Around You
sketches.description: A three-voice canon over a D pedal: the first violin enters ahead-left, the second a bar later ahead-right, and the viola two bars later from behind you, while the cello stays in front.

sketches.name: Nocturne in Phase
sketches.description: A piano nocturne in E-flat sings in the centre of your head while a string pad underneath steps from in phase to 90 and 180 degrees, spreading from a point into a haze around you. Soft rain falls outside, uncorrelated in each ear. On speakers the 180-degree bars of the pad nearly vanish.

sketches.name: Divided Violins
sketches.description: After the finale of Tchaikovsky's Sixth Symphony: a falling melody and a rising countermelody are shared between the first violins in the left ear and the seconds in the right, swapping on every note. Each ear alone plays a jagged line; many listeners instead hear smooth lines grouped by pitch.

sketches.name: Chorale in Delays
sketches.description: A four-part chorale in G whose voices are placed only by tiny delays between the ears: soprano left, alto right, tenor slightly left, bass dead centre. An organ underneath is widened by a longer, precedence-range delay that grows bar by bar.
sketches.source:
setcpm(60/4)

// Under about 0.7 ms a delay between the ears moves a voice sideways
// Negative values lean left, positive values lean right; the bass has no delay at all
soprano: note("<[g4 g4 a4 b4] [c5 b4 a4@2] [b4 c5 d5 c5] [b4 a4 g4@2]>")
  .s("ooh").itd(-.5).attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.2)
alto: note("<[d4 e4 f#4 g4] [g4 g4 f#4@2] [g4 g4 g4 a4] [g4 f#4 d4@2]>")
  .s("ooh").itd(.5).attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.18)
tenor: note("<[b3 c4 d4 d4] [e4 d4 d4@2] [d4 e4 d4 e4] [d4 d4 b3@2]>")
  .s("ooh").itd(-.25).attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.18)
bass: note("<[g2 c3 d3 g2] [c3 g2 d3@2] [g2 c3 b2 a2] [d3 d3 g2@2]>")
  .s("ooh").attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.22)

// From about 1 to 30 ms the organ stays on the leading side but grows wider each bar
organ: note("<[g2,d3,g3] [c3,g3,c4] [g2,d3,b3] [d3,a3,d4]>").s("sawtooth").timbre("organ")
  .itd("<1 6 12 20>").lpf(900).attack(.4).sustain(.8).release(1).space("church").gain(.1)

sketches.name: Adagio in Cents
sketches.description: A slow string adagio in B-flat minor. The string orchestra's ears drift apart in cents, two bars at a time: 2 cents beats slowly, 6 and 12 shimmer like a larger section and 30 blooms into a chorus, while the solo violin and cellos stay true in the centre.

sketches.name: Split Toccata
sketches.description: An organ toccata in D minor with spectral fusion: the manual's arpeggios send alternate partials to each ear, and the chords split lows from highs at 600 Hz. Neither ear hears the whole organ; together, and in mono, it sounds complete. The pedal stays centred.
sketches.source:
setcpm(108/4)

// earsplit("harmonics") alternates the partials between the ears: each ear hears a thinner, hollow organ
manual: n("0 4 9 4 7 4 9 4").add("<0 -1 -2 -3>").scale("D:minor").transpose(12)
  .s("sawtooth").timbre("organ").earsplit("harmonics")
  .attack(.005).decay(.15).sustain(.4).release(.1).lpf(3000).space("church").gain(.18)

// earsplit("bands") sends the chords' lows to one ear and highs to the other
chords: note("<[d4,f4,a4,d5] [c4,e4,g4,c5] [bb3,d4,f4,bb4] [a3,c4,e4,a4]>").struct("x ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ x ~")
  .s("sawtooth").timbre("organ").earsplit("bands").splitfreq(600)
  .attack(.02).sustain(.6).release(.5).lpf(2400).space("church").gain(.14)

// The pedal, the same in both ears
pedal: note("<d2 c2 bb1 a1>").s("sawtooth").timbre("organ").lpf(500)
  .attack(.05).sustain(.8).release(.6).space("church").gain(.26)

sketches.name: Rotary Chorale
sketches.description: A chorale prelude: a reed stop sings the hymn in the centre while the accompanying organ chords turn their interaural phase, once every four seconds, then every two, then once and twice a second, so the harmony rolls around inside your head. All rates stay below 3 Hz.

sketches.name: Twilight Quartet
sketches.description: A string quartet in A minor where nothing is panned, yet the first violin's brightness wanders between the ears: a low-pass on each ear alone sweeps in opposite directions. The viola is thinner on the right, where a high-pass cuts its body.

sketches.name: Delta Lullaby
sketches.description: Headphones on: an original cradle song in 3/4 on a music box floating above your head, over a 2 Hz binaural drone in the delta range, below the rates that trigger a pulse warning. A soft hum and far-off crickets keep it company.
